purpose: Vismodegib is used to treat a type of skin cancer called basal cell carcinoma that has spread to other parts of the body or cannot be treated with surgery or radiation. It is a pill that targets the cancer directly. Your doctor has determined this treatment is the best option for your specific situation.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have an abnormal signaling pathway called the Hedgehog pathway that tells them to keep growing out of control. Vismodegib works like a roadblock by attaching to a specific protein in this pathway and shutting it down. This stops the cancer cells from getting the signal they need to grow and spread.
common_side_effects: Muscle cramps (very common), hair loss, loss of appetite or weight loss, fatigue or tiredness, nausea, diarrhea, constipation, taste changes or loss of taste, and joint pain. Most of these are manageable but let your doctor or pharmacist know if they bother you.
warnings: This medication can cause serious birth defects or death to an unborn baby — do not use if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Both men and women must use reliable birth control during treatment and for a period after stopping. Women should not breastfeed while taking this drug. Do not donate blood while on vismodegib. Call your doctor right away if you experience unusual muscle weakness or pain.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 150 mg capsule taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Try to take it at the same time each day. Swallow the capsule whole — do not open, crush, or chew it. If you miss a dose, just skip it and take your next dose as scheduled; do not double up.
